Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: first-person point-and-click castle exploration game background. Generate ONE full-bleed landscape 1536x1024 image, 3:2. Fine realistic painted environmental concept art of the SAME inhabited medium-sized western fantasy lord's castle, with crisp legible architectural edges and rich but natural material textures. Pale warm-gray limestone ashlar, restrained pointed stone arches, textured dark oak, small aged bronze fittings, muted wine-red textiles where appropriate. Believable well-maintained castle proportions and rigid coherent perspective, refined but modest rather than a royal palace. Standing eye-level camera with natural wide field of view, foreground and middle-distance depth. Soft cool daylight balanced by restrained warm household light where appropriate, calm inhabited atmosphere. No people, readable text, signage, emblems, UI, navigation arrows, hotspot outlines, return-button graphic, watermark, collage, modern objects, excessive bloom or magical effects. The picture must be a finished game environment, not a map or cutaway.
Scene: the lord's DAILY DINING ROOM on the ground floor, distinctly more intimate than the high great hall. Camera has just entered from the ground-floor gallery through its pointed dark-oak double doors; that entrance is BEHIND the viewer and outside the frame. Show a comfortable one-storey stone room around 3.8m high, with substantial dark oak ceiling beams, pale limestone pointed window recesses, and cool soft daylight entering from tall leaded windows on the LEFT. A generously made dark oak dining table occupies CENTER LEFT, set for a small household with roughly six places: restrained plain ceramic plates, simple bronze utensils, folded natural linen, a few cups, one low unlit candle arrangement and a small ceramic serving jug. Keep the table recognizably domestic and human-scaled rather than a feast for dozens. Sober high-backed wooden chairs with muted wine-red seat upholstery, an understated worn rug under the table, a practical oak sideboard against a free wall, and a modest stone fireplace in the rear LEFT wall complete a lived-in noble home. Clear open floor in the RIGHT foreground leads around the table.
EXACTLY ONE VISIBLE onward doorway: a CLOSED SINGLE dark-oak SERVICE DOOR to the KITCHEN, in a restrained pointed pale-stone frame on the RIGHT rear wall, approximately x=73%-88%, y=22%-83%. Give it a simple aged-bronze ring handle, clean full arch, jambs and visible threshold, no labels. This door must be clearly separated from the fireplace and the sideboard, with an unobstructed walking path; do not hide it behind chairs. It is narrower and plainer than the great hall's or gallery's formal double doors but a full normal human doorway. The room's other exit, back to the gallery, remains behind the camera. Do not add garden doors or other entrances. No upper gallery, stairs, throne, enormous banquet table, glowing chandelier excess, chandelier blocking the kitchen door, open kitchen counter, people or newly invented heraldry.
